key_insight: A sharp-crack deep energy method is extended to jointly solve transient heat conduction and thermo-mechanical crack growth by encoding the crack directly into the neural inputs and advancing the crack with a fracture criterion.
engineering_relevance: This enables physics-informed prediction of crack initiation and path evolution under thermal, mechanical, and combined loading without introducing a phase-field regularization length.
method: Two neural networks approximate temperature and displacement on a cracked domain using a discontinuous scalar crack embedding.
The displacement field is further enriched near the crack tip with a Williams expansion with trainable amplitudes.
Training alternates minimization of conduction and thermoelastic energy with Monte Carlo sampling, while crack advance uses interaction-integral SIFs and the maximum hoop-stress criterion.
evidence_signal: The method matches a published thermal edge-crack stress intensity factor within 0.11% and reproduces benchmark crack initiation and paths on graded and cruciform specimens.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on careful crack-tip sampling, contour-radius checks for SIF extraction, and stable coupling between thermal and mechanical updates.
paper_title: An extended deep energy method for thermo-mechanical crack propagation
